qe: Why did Robert Hooke's landmark observation of cork cells in 1665 reveal only empty, rigid compartments rather than functional, fluid-filled metabolic units?
qh: 1665 में रॉबर्ट हुक द्वारा कॉर्क कोशिकाओं के ऐतिहासिक अवलोकन में कार्यात्मक, तरल से भरे चयापचय (metabolic) इकाइयों के बजाय केवल खाली, कठोर डिब्बे ही क्यों दिखाई दिए?
o: The primitive magnifying lenses lacked the resolving power to pass through the lipid bilayer.
Cork is derived from the dead outer bark of a tree which has completely lost its living protoplasm.
The specimen was extracted during the dormant winter phase of the plant's seasonal cycle.
High concentrations of ocean electrolytes inside the bark had caused complete cellular lysis.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because the absence of cellular machinery was due to tissue biology, not just optical limits. Option 2 is correct because cork is a plant substance obtained from the outer bark of woody trees. These mature cells undergo programmed death, leaving behind empty, rigid cell walls composed of suberized cellulose. Hence, Hooke only observed empty spaces resembling 'little rooms' (cells). Option 3 is a distractor introducing seasonal plant dormancy [a period of suspended growth and metabolic activity]. Option 4 incorrectly attempts to link the phenomenon to electrolyte-induced cell lysis [the disintegration of a cell by rupture of the cell wall or membrane], which is irrelevant to natural cork structure.

qe: Which of the following cellular milestones is accurately paired with the scientist who discovered or coined it?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कोशिकीय मील का पत्थर (cellular milestone) उस वैज्ञानिक के साथ सटीक रूप से सुमेलित है जिसने इसकी खोज की या इसका नामकरण किया था?
o: Discovery of the free-living cell — Robert Brown
Coining the structural term 'Protoplasm' — Purkinje
Discovery of the intracellular Nucleus — Anton van Leeuwenhoek
Formulation of the rule that all cells arise from pre-existing cells — Schleiden
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because free-living cells in pond water were discovered by Leeuwenhoek (1674), not Robert Brown. Option 2 is correct because Purkinje in 1839 coined the term 'protoplasm' to describe the living fluid substance [the complex colloidal matrix comprising both cytoplasm and nucleoplasm] inside the cell. Option 3 is incorrect because the nucleus was discovered by Robert Brown in 1831. Option 4 is incorrect because the lineage law (omnis cellula e cellula) was proposed by Rudolf Virchow (1855), not Schleiden.

qe: What fundamental biological truth did Rudolf Virchow contribute in 1855 to expand the classical Cell Theory previously formulated by Schleiden and Schwann?
qh: रुडोल्फ विरचो ने 1855 में श्लेडेन और श्वान द्वारा पहले से तैयार किए गए क्लासिक कोशिका सिद्धांत (Cell Theory) का विस्तार करने के लिए किस मौलिक जैविक सत्य का योगदान दिया?
o: Cells achieve absolute division of labour through specialized membrane channels.
All cells arise exclusively from the division of pre-existing cells.
The nucleus is the absolute site for structural protein synthesis.
Unicellular organisms possess a fundamentally different protoplasmic fluid than multicellular ones.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because structural division of labour was understood through general observation, not Virchow's specific expansion. Option 2 is correct because Schleiden and Schwann described cells as the building blocks of life but couldn't explain how new cells formed. Virchow expanded the theory by postulating that all cells arise from pre-existing cells via cellular replication [the process by which a parent cell divides to generate new daughter cells]. Option 3 is incorrect because protein translation occurs in the ribosomes/cytoplasm, not directly inside the nucleus. Option 4 is incorrect because protoplasmic composition is universally shared across unicellular and multicellular lines.

qe: When viewing onion peel cells extracted from bulbs of vastly different physical sizes under a light microscope, what structural pattern is observed regarding cellular dimensions?
qh: एक प्रकाश सूक्ष्मदर्शी के नीचे अत्यधिक भिन्न भौतिक आकारों के कंदों (bulbs) से निकाली गई प्याज के छिलके की कोशिकाओं को देखने पर, कोशिकीय आयामों (cellular dimensions) के संबंध में कौन सा संरचनात्मक पैटर्न देखा जाता है?
o: Larger bulbs possess significantly larger individual cells to support the extra weight.
The cells look structurally identical, regardless of the macro-size of the onion bulb they came from.
Cells from smaller bulbs lack a fully formed cell membrane due to developmental limits.
The individual cell size fluctuates violently based on the total surface area of the roots.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because organ scaling is driven by cell numbers, not individual cell enlargement. Option 2 is correct because the text explicitly notes that onion cells from different-sized bulbs look exactly the same under a microscope. Cells represent the baseline building units [the smallest structural and functional modules of an organism], and their structural blueprints remain uniform within a species. Option 3 is incorrect because all functional plant cells possess a complete plasma membrane. Option 4 is incorrect because root surface area regulates water flux but does not alter the genetic geometry of specialized epidermal tissue cells.

qe: Which of the following organisms represents an entity where a single, isolated cell constitutes the entire independent living individual?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा जीव एक ऐसी इकाई का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है जहाँ एक एकल, पृथक कोशिका ही संपूर्ण स्वतंत्र जीवित जीव का निर्माण करती है?
o: Rhizopus soft fungi
Chlamydomonas
Multicellular sub-aerial plants
Macro-invertebrate animals
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because Rhizopus is a filamentous multicellular fungus. Option 2 is correct because the source text lists Amoeba, Chlamydomonas, Paramecium, and bacteria as unicellular organisms [organisms consisting of a single independent cell that carries out all metabolic and reproductive cycles]. Option 3 and Option 4 are incorrect because advanced plants and animals are multicellular systems exhibiting systematic tissue specialization.

qe: The technological invention of which instrument in the year 1940 marked a critical breakthrough that allowed biologists to map the detailed inner structure of cell organelles?
qh: वर्ष 1940 में किस उपकरण के तकनीकी आविष्कार ने एक महत्वपूर्ण सफलता दर्ज की, जिसने जीवविज्ञानी को कोशिकांगों (cell organelles) की विस्तृत आंतरिक संरचना का मानचित्रण करने की अनुमति दी?
o: Phase-contrast compound optical lens array
The Electron Microscope
Fluorescent UV-light scattering scanning systems
Digital stereomicroscopic reflection grids
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because optical phase arrays improve contrast in living specimens but lack sub-nanometer resolution. Option 2 is correct because the textbook highlights that the discovery of the electron microscope [a high-resolution imaging instrument using accelerated electron beams instead of light photons] in 1940 finally bypassed the physical limits of light wavelengths, allowing scientists to see ultra-small intracellular organelles. Option 3 and Option 4 are modern structural imaging tools that do not correlate with the specific 1940 benchmark.

qe: What is the primary evolutionary driver responsible for the diverse morphological shapes and sizes of different cells within the human body, such as elongated nerve cells?
qh: मानव शरीर के भीतर विभिन्न कोशिकाओं के विविध रूपात्मक आकारों (morphological shapes) और आकारों के लिए जिम्मेदार प्राथमिक विकासवादी चालक (evolutionary driver) क्या है, जैसे कि लंबी तंत्रिका कोशिकाएं?
o: The localized variation in tissue temperature inside different internal organs.
The specific physiological function that the individual cell type is specialized to perform.
The mechanical pressure exerted by the surrounding dead skeletal elements.
The random distribution of lipids across the baseline extracellular fluid.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because internal organs maintain a uniform homeostatic core temperature. Option 2 is correct because a cell's shape and size are optimized for its unique function. For example, a human nerve cell is elongated to rapidly conduct bio-electric nerve impulses [signals transmitted along neural axons to communicate with distant body parts], while an Amoeba has a dynamic, changing shape to capture food. Option 3 is incorrect because skeletal support structures do not determine individual cellular geometry. Option 4 is incorrect because cellular design is genetically controlled, not a random physical outcome of lipid distribution.

qe: How does a single-celled, isolated organism like a Paramecium accomplish 'division of labour' without possessing specialized tissues or complex organ systems?
qh: एककोशिकीय, पृथक जीव जैसे कि पैरामिशियम (Paramecium) विशिष्ट ऊतकों या जटिल अंग प्रणालियों के बिना 'श्रम का विभाजन' (division of labour) कैसे पूरा करता है?
o: By constantly splitting its main body into transient multicellular colonies.
Through specific intracellular components called organelles that perform distinct biochemical tasks.
By relying completely on passive thermal currents in external pond water.
By alternating between heterotrophic and autotrophic phases every metabolic cycle.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because unicellular organisms remain strictly individual and do not rely on temporary colony formation for daily division of labour. Option 2 is correct because division of labour exists inside a single cell through cell organelles [sub-cellular specialized structures encased within the plasma membrane]. One organelle synthesizes new material, another manages energy conversions, and another handles waste disposal, keeping the cell alive. Option 3 is incorrect because passive external currents cannot drive specialized internal metabolic pathways. Option 4 is incorrect because metabolic flexibility does not explain structural division of labour.

qe: Why is the plasma membrane of a living cell scientifically designated as a 'selectively permeable' barrier?
qh: किसी जीवित कोशिका की प्लाज्मा झिल्ली (plasma membrane) को वैज्ञानिक रूप से 'चयनात्मक पारगम्य' (selectively permeable) अवरोध क्यों कहा जाता है?
o: It allows the unrestricted passage of water molecules while completely blocking all gases.
It permits the entry and exit of some specific materials while actively preventing the movement of others.
It transforms into a fully static, solid wall when exposed to acidic extracellular fluids.
It allows only inorganic mineral ions to cross via passive diffusion processes.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because gases like $CO_2$ and $O_2$ pass through the membrane easily via diffusion. Option 2 is correct because the plasma membrane actively regulates its internal environment. It allows chosen nutrients and gases to pass while blocking toxic or unwanted compounds from entering or leaving. This property defines a selectively permeable membrane [a biological barrier that discriminates between different chemical solutes based on specific cellular transport systems]. Option 3 describes chemical denaturing, not selective permeability. Option 4 is incorrect because organic molecules also cross the membrane through specialized transporters.

qe: Which of the following physical mechanisms represents the spontaneous movement of gaseous molecules like Carbon Dioxide ($CO_2$) across the cellular membrane from a region of high concentration to low concentration?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भौतिक तंत्र (physical mechanism) उच्च सांद्रता वाले क्षेत्र से कम सांद्रता वाले क्षेत्र में सेलुलर झिल्ली के पार कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड ($CO_2$) जैसे गैसीय अणुओं की सहज गति (spontaneous movement) का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है?
o: Active molecular pumping fueled by ATP hydrolysis
Invagination via specialized endocytic vesicles
Simple passive Diffusion
Retrograde bulk Exocytosis
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because metabolic energy (ATP) is not expended during the passive transport of small respiratory gases. Option 2 is incorrect because endocytosis [the process of engulfing particulate matter by infolding the plasma membrane] is meant for larger solids or liquids, not individual gas molecules. Option 3 is correct because $CO_2$ is a metabolic waste that accumulates inside cells, creating a high internal concentration. It naturally moves down its concentration gradient out into the lower concentration environment via simple diffusion [the passive net movement of particles from high to low concentration driven by intrinsic kinetic energy]. Option 4 is incorrect because exocytosis expels larger cellular secretions in bulk vesicles.

qe: The biophysical movement of water molecules across a selectively permeable cell membrane down its concentration gradient is defined as which process?
qh: चयनात्मक रूप से पारगम्य कोशिका झिल्ली के पार पानी के अणुओं की उसकी सांद्रता प्रवणता (concentration gradient) के अनुकूल जैव-भौतिक गति (biophysical movement) को किस प्रक्रिया के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है?
o: Active peptide-facilitated transport
Osmosis
Phagocytic engulfment
Sub-stomatal hydrostatic pressure filtration
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because water movement across standard gradients does not require peptide-pump energy inputs. Option 2 is correct because the text explicitly defines osmosis as the specific case of diffusion involving water molecules passing through a selectively permeable membrane [a barrier that blocks solute movement but allows solvent migration] from a region of high water concentration to low water concentration. Option 3 is incorrect because phagocytosis is a type of endocytosis used to ingest large solid particles. Option 4 is a botanical macro-process that does not define membrane-level water kinetics.

qe: What precise physiological response will occur if an animal cell is placed into a hypertonic solution containing a lower concentration of water than the intracellular cytoplasm?
qh: यदि एक जंतु कोशिका को एक हाइपरटोनिक घोल (hypertonic solution) में रखा जाता है जिसमें इंट्रासेलुलर साइटोप्लाज्म की तुलना में पानी की सांद्रता कम होती है, तो क्या सटीक शारीरिक प्रतिक्रिया होगी?
o: Water will rapidly flood into the cell, causing it to swell and burst.
Water will cross the membrane equally in both directions, keeping the size perfectly static.
More water will leave the cell than enters it, causing the cell to shrink.
The cell will immediately activate protein synthesis to stiffen the outer lipid layer.
e: Explanation: Option 1 describes the outcome of a hypotonic environment where water rushes inward. Option 2 describes an isotonic solution where net flux is zero. Option 3 is correct because when a cell is surrounded by a hypertonic solution [a medium with a higher solute concentration and lower water concentration relative to the cell's interior], osmotic forces drive water out of the cell across the selectively permeable membrane. This net loss of water causes the entire animal cell to shrink. Option 4 is incorrect because cellular shrinking under osmotic stress is a physical water-loss phenomenon, not an active structural stiffening process.

qe: When an animal cell is placed in an external environment that is very dilute, causing a net influx of water that makes the cell swell up, what type of solution is the cell exposed to?
qh: जब एक जंतु कोशिका को बाहरी वातावरण में रखा जाता है जो बहुत पतला (dilute) होता है, जिससे पानी का शुद्ध प्रवेश (net influx) होता है जो कोशिका को फुला देता है, तो कोशिका किस प्रकार के घोल के संपर्क में आती है?
o: A highly concentrated Hypertonic solution
An balanced Isotonic solution
A very dilute Hypotonic solution
A saturated organic solute dispersion
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because a hypertonic solution draws water *out* of the cell, causing it to shrink. Option 2 is incorrect because an isotonic medium matches the cell's internal water balance, resulting in zero size change. Option 3 is correct because a very dilute external solution has a higher water concentration than the cell's cytoplasm. This is defined as a hypotonic solution [a solution with lower osmotic pressure and higher water potential than the reference cell fluid]. Water moves down its gradient into the cell, causing it to swell. Option 4 is a generic chemistry term that does not describe osmotic tonicity.

qe: Which of the following biological phenomena serves as a prominent real-world example of the physical principle of osmosis in terrestrial vegetation?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा जैविक घटना स्थलीय वनस्पतियों (terrestrial vegetation) में ऑस्मोसिस (परासरण) के भौतिक सिद्धांत का एक प्रमुख वास्तविक दुनिया का उदाहरण है?
o: The transport of gaseous carbon dioxide through epidermal stomatal openings.
The absorption of groundwater by the roots of terrestrial plants.
The volatile evaporation of water vapor from leaf surfaces into the drier air.
The synthesis of structural cellulose molecules within young growing shoots.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because stomatal gas transport is driven by gaseous diffusion gradients, not liquid solvent movement. Option 2 is correct because the source text explicitly notes that the absorption of water by plant roots from the soil is a direct physiological manifestation of osmosis [the passive diffusion of water through a semi-permeable membrane]. The root cells maintain a higher solute concentration than the soil moisture, driving water inward. Option 3 describes transpiration via evaporation, which is driven by vapor pressure differences. Option 4 is a metabolic pathway for carbohydrate synthesis, not a transport mechanism.

qe: What are the primary organic structural building blocks that compose the highly flexible matrix of the plasma membrane?
qh: प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के अत्यधिक लचीले मैट्रिक्स (flexible matrix) का निर्माण करने वाले प्राथमिक कार्बनिक संरचनात्मक निर्माण खंड (organic structural building blocks) कौन से हैं?
o: Cellulose fibrils and specialized structural pectins
Lipids and Proteins
Chitin arrays interspersed with insoluble starches
Nucleic acid strands wrapped around glycogen grids
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because cellulose and pectin form the rigid plant cell wall [an outer non-living protective layer], not the plasma membrane. Option 2 is correct because the textbook explicitly states that the flexible plasma membrane is composed of organic molecules classified as lipids and proteins. These molecules organize into a fluid mosaic bilayer that controls molecular traffic. Option 3 describes components found in fungal walls and arthropod exoskeletons. Option 4 is incorrect because nucleic acids (DNA/RNA) store genetic code inside the cell and are not structural building blocks of the outer membrane.

qe: The inherent structural flexibility of the cell membrane enables single-celled organisms like Amoeba to actively engulf food and other large materials from their external environment. What is this process called?
qh: कोशिका झिल्ली का अंतर्निहित संरचनात्मक लचीलापन अमीबा जैसे एककोशिकीय जीवों को अपने बाहरी वातावरण से भोजन और अन्य बड़े पदार्थों को सक्रिय रूप से निगलने (engulf) में सक्षम बनाता है। इस प्रक्रिया को क्या कहा जाता है?
o: Plasmolysis
Exocytosis
Endocytosis
Hypertonic condensation
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because plasmolysis is the shrinking of plant protoplasm away from the cell wall due to water loss. Option 2 is incorrect because exocytosis is the process of expelling vesicle contents out of the cell. Option 3 is correct because the text explicitly defines endocytosis [a cellular transport mechanism where the flexible plasma membrane folds inward to form a vesicle, bringing external mass into the cell] as the process Amoeba uses to acquire its food from the surrounding water. Option 4 is a fabricated term combining unrelated osmotic concepts.

qe: When a cell must transport nutrient molecules across its plasma membrane *against* their natural concentration gradients, what specific resource is directly required?
qh: जब एक कोशिका को पोषक अणुओं को उनकी प्राकृतिक सांद्रता प्रवणता (concentration gradients) के *विपरीत* अपनी प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के पार ले जाना होता है, तो किस विशिष्ट संसाधन की सीधे आवश्यकता होती है?
o: Extracellular cellulose structural stabilizers
Energy expended in the form of Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)
Continuous thermal convection currents from pond water
High concentrations of inactive dissolved sugar solutes
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because cellulose provides external structural support and does not power chemical transport. Option 2 is correct because the text notes that while gases and water move passively via diffusion down concentration gradients, the transport of other specific molecules against gradients requires energy in the form of ATP [Adenosine Triphosphate: the primary chemical energy currency used by cells to perform active metabolic work]. Option 3 is incorrect because external thermal currents drive passive kinetic collisions, not active transport. Option 4 is incorrect because passive sugar gradients cannot drive the movement of other molecules against their own gradients.

qe: If a microscopic analysis reveals three universal structural attributes—a plasma membrane, a central nuclear region, and a cytoplasmic matrix—how is this functional unit classified?
qh: यदि एक सूक्ष्मदर्शी विश्लेषण से तीन सार्वभौमिक संरचनात्मक विशेषताओं—एक प्लाज्मा झिल्ली, एक केंद्रीय केंद्रक क्षेत्र (nuclear region) और एक साइटोप्लाज्मिक मैट्रिक्स—का पता चलता है, तो इस कार्यात्मक इकाई को कैसे वर्गीकृत किया जाता है?
o: An abiotic proteinaceous coacervate complex
A complete biological cell capable of executing all life processes
An inert metabolic capsule typical of pathogenic viruses
A non-compartmentalized syncytial mass of extracellular fluid
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because coacervates are non-living droplets that lack genetic nuclei and organized membranes. Option 2 is correct because the text states that these three features (plasma membrane, nucleus, and cytoplasm) are found in almost every cell. Together with internal organelles, they form the basic functional unit called the cell, which can live independently and perform all basic biological functions. Option 3 is incorrect because viruses are non-cellular structures that lack a true cytoplasm, plasma membrane, and internal organelles. Option 4 is incorrect because the presence of these distinct structures explicitly confirms internal organization.

qe: What universal rule does the textbook establish regarding the distribution of internal cell organelles across the diverse kingdoms of living organisms?
qh: जीवित जीवों के विभिन्न जगतों (kingdoms) में आंतरिक कोशिकांगों (cell organelles) के वितरण के संबंध में पाठ्यपुस्तक कौन सा सार्वभौमिक नियम स्थापित करती है?
o: Organelles display completely different chemical building elements in every separate species.
All cells are found to have the same basic organelles, regardless of their organismic source or specific function.
Unicellular organisms lack functional organelles entirely and rely on naked cytoplasm.
Organelles dissolve into raw lipids whenever the host organism enters a rest cycle.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because the basic molecular composition of organelles is highly conserved across life. Option 2 is correct because the text explicitly highlights a fundamental biological fact: all cells share the same basic organelles, no matter what specialized function they perform or what organism they belong to. This demonstrates a shared evolutionary foundation for cellular life. Option 3 is incorrect because single-celled organisms like Paramecium contain specialized organelles to manage their internal division of labour. Option 4 is an scientifically inaccurate distractor that contradicts cellular stability.

qe: Which of the following environmental variations directly affects or modulates the rate and net direction of water molecule passage across the selectively permeable plasma membrane?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा पर्यावरणीय परिवर्तन चयनात्मक रूप से पारगम्य प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के पार पानी के अणुओं के मार्ग की दर और शुद्ध दिशा को सीधे प्रभावित या नियंत्रित (modulate) करता है?
o: The concentration of gaseous atmospheric nitrogen surrounding the dry leaves.
The amount of solute substance dissolved in the surrounding water solution.
The mechanical thickness of the tree's outer secondary cork layer.
The metabolic production of structural chitin fibers inside the internal vacuole.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because atmospheric nitrogen gas concentrations do not drive liquid water kinetics across internal cell membranes. Option 2 is correct because the text states that the movement of water across the plasma membrane is directly affected by the amount of substance (solute) dissolved in the water. The dissolved solute concentration determines the water potential gradient [the thermodynamic driving force that regulates osmotic flow from high to low water availability], changing the system's kinetics. Option 3 is incorrect because outer dead cork protects the tree but does not regulate the microscopic osmotic kinetics of living inner cells. Option 4 is incorrect because chitin is not synthesized inside vacuoles to control membrane-level osmosis.

qe: Why do completely dead plant tissue cells fail to demonstrate the process of net influx or efflux of water molecules when placed in an extreme osmotic gradient?
qh: पानी के अत्यधिक परासरणी प्रवणता (osmotic gradient) में रखे जाने पर पूरी तरह से मृत पादप ऊतक कोशिकाएं जल अणुओं के शुद्ध प्रवेश या निकास की प्रक्रिया को प्रदर्शित करने में क्यों विफल रहती हैं?
o: Dead cell walls become immediately impermeable to both water and dissolved gases.
The physical process of osmosis requires a living protoplasm and an intact, functional cell membrane.
Dead plant cells generate immediate mechanical counter-pressure that stops water flow.
The chromatin material undergoes instantaneous ionization, blocking the nuclear pores.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because cell walls remain freely permeable [allowing unrestricted passage of water and solutes] even after cellular death. Option 2 is correct because the source text explicitly states that only living cells, and not dead cells, are able to absorb water by osmosis. Osmosis is a specialized case of diffusion across a selectively permeable plasma membrane [a living dynamic lipid-protein bilayer], which loses its selective properties and structural integrity upon cell death. Option 3 is incorrect because turgor counter-pressure [mechanical pressure exerted by the cell wall against the expanding protoplast] can only be generated by a swelling, living cell. Option 4 is an scientifically inaccurate distractor involving chromatin ionization [the conversion of DNA-protein complexes into charged ions], which has no mechanical bearing on osmotic transport.

qe: Plant, fungal, and bacterial cells can easily survive inside highly dilute (hypotonic) external media without bursting. Which specific mechanical attribute protects them compared to animal cells?
qh: पादप, कवक (fungal), और बैक्टीरिया की कोशिकाएं बिना फटे अत्यधिक पतले (hypotonic) बाहरी माध्यम में आसानी से जीवित रह सकती हैं। जंतु कोशिकाओं की तुलना में कौन सा विशिष्ट यांत्रिक गुण (mechanical attribute) उनकी रक्षा करता है?
o: The presence of a rigid cell wall that exerts an equal counter-pressure against the swollen cell.
The dynamic activation of active lipid biogenesis inside the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
The spontaneous breakdown of dense intracellular vacuoles into tiny porous vesicles.
The immediate transport of excess incoming water molecules through the nuclear pore complex.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is correct because when plant, fungal, or bacterial cells are placed in hypotonic media [a solution with a lower solute concentration and higher water potential than the cell interior], water enters via osmosis, causing the cell to swell. The rigid cell wall limits this expansion by exerting an equal and opposite mechanical pressure against the swollen protoplast, preventing cell lysis [the structural bursting of a cell due to osmotic swelling]. Animal cells lack this wall and burst under similar stress. Option 2 is incorrect because lipid biogenesis [the metabolic synthesis of membrane fats] is a long-term growth process, not an immediate mechanical defense. Option 3 is incorrect because plant vacuoles remain large and full of cell sap to maintain rigidity rather than breaking up. Option 4 is incorrect because nuclear pores facilitate nucleocytoplasmic transport [molecular exchange between the nucleus and cytoplasm] and do not act as bulk water pumps.

qe: When preparing a temporary mount of onion peel cells, different intracellular regions appear differentially stained under a light microscope. What is the biochemical reason for this phenomenon?
qh: प्याज के छिलके की कोशिकाओं का अस्थायी माउंट (temporary mount) तैयार करते समय, विभिन्न अंतःकोशकीय क्षेत्र प्रकाश सूक्ष्मदर्शी के नीचे अलग-अलग रंग के दिखाई देते हैं। इस घटना का जैव-रासायनिक कारण क्या है?
o: The unequal distribution of electron beams generated by primitive light optics.
The differential chemical composition of various cellular regions causing varied dye binding.
The rapid structural decay of the outermost cellulosic wall upon exposure to iodine.
The active excretion of dye molecules by specialized contractile food vacuoles.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because light microscopes utilize photons [light particles], not electron beams, and optical distribution does not cause region-specific staining. Option 2 is correct because according to the text, different regions of cells get coloured differentially when exposed to stains like iodine, safranin, or methylene blue. This occurs because the varied chemical composition [the unique mix of lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates] across organelles and structural zones alters their affinity to bind specific chemical dyes. Option 3 is incorrect because iodine acts as a mild contrasting agent and does not cause rapid structural decay of the cell wall. Option 4 is incorrect because dye uptake in fixed temporary mounts is a passive biochemical staining phenomenon, not active vacuolar clearing.

qe: Which of the following chemical solutions can be utilized as alternative microscopic stains to clearly differentiate the internal structural components of plant tissues?
qh: पादप ऊतकों के आंतरिक संरचनात्मक घटकों को स्पष्ट रूप से अलग करने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किस रासायनिक घोल का उपयोग वैकल्पिक सूक्ष्मदर्शी रंजक (microscopic stains) के रूप में किया जा सकता है?
o: Weak silver nitrate and concentrated organic lipid emulsions
Safranin solution or Methylene blue solution
Purified adenosine triphosphate and cellular sap extracts
Suberized iodine crystals dissolved in liquid chloroform
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because silver nitrate is specific to Golgi's nerve staining technique ('black reaction') and lipid emulsions are not contrasting stains. Option 2 is correct because the source text explicitly notes that apart from iodine solution, biologists can also successfully utilize safranin solution [a red biological stain used for plant tissues and cell walls] or methylene blue solution [a popular basic dye used to highlight animal and plant nuclei] to stain cells for microscopic evaluation. Option 3 is incorrect because ATP is an energy currency molecule and cell sap is an internal vacuolar fluid; neither are staining reagents. Option 4 is a fabricated distractor combining unrelated chemical terms.

qe: What structural feature characterizes the covering of a eukaryotic nucleus, and how does it facilitate communication with the surrounding cytoplasm?
qh: एक यूकेरियोटिक केंद्रक (eukaryotic nucleus) के आवरण की संरचनात्मक विशेषता क्या है, और यह आसपास के साइटोप्लाज्म के साथ संचार को कैसे सुगम बनाता है?
o: A porous single-layered membrane that permits the direct passage of intact chromosomes.
A highly porous double-layered membrane that allows the transfer of specific materials.
An impermeable lipid sheath that completely isolates genetic DNA molecules.
A dynamic cellulosic wall that expands during metabolic cellular reproduction.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because the nuclear envelope is a double-layered structure, and it never permits intact chromosomes to leave the nucleus. Option 2 is correct because the nucleus possesses a double-layered covering called the nuclear membrane, which contains specialized pores. These nuclear pores act as selective molecular gates that allow the regulated transfer of macromolecular materials [such as RNA and proteins] between the nuclear interior and the external cytoplasm. Option 3 is incorrect because an impermeable membrane would block genetic transcription and cause cell death. Option 4 is incorrect because cell walls are external plant structures, not nuclear membranes.

qe: A student examines a non-dividing eukaryotic cell under a microscope. How will the genetic material (DNA) inside the nucleus structurally present itself during this specific lifecycle stage?
qh: एक छात्र सूक्ष्मदर्शी के नीचे एक गैर-विभाजित (non-dividing) यूकेरियोटिक कोशिका का परीक्षण करता है। इस विशिष्ट जीवन चक्र चरण के दौरान केंद्रक के अंदर अनुवांशिक पदार्थ (DNA) संरचनात्मक रूप से कैसे प्रस्तुत होगा?
o: As highly condensed, distinct, rod-shaped structures called chromosomes.
As an entangled mass of thread-like structures visible as chromatin material.
As tiny, isolated circular packets scattered throughout the outer cytoplasm.
As naked, membrane-enclosed fluid sacks designated as nucleoids.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because highly condensed, rod-shaped chromosomes are only visible when the cell is actively about to divide. Option 2 is correct because in a cell which is not undergoing active mitotic division, the genomic DNA molecules remain uncoiled and spread out as an entangled mass of thread-like structures called chromatin material [the relaxed complex of DNA and histone proteins]. Option 3 is incorrect because genomic eukaryotic DNA is held strictly inside the nucleus, not scattered in the cytoplasm. Option 4 describes prokaryotic genetic organization, not eukaryotic cell stages.

qe: What are the fundamental architectural components that chemically make up the structural units known as chromosomes?
qh: गुणसूत्रों (chromosomes) के रूप में जानी जाने वाली संरचनात्मक इकाइयों को रासायनिक रूप से बनाने वाले मौलिक संरचनात्मक घटक क्या हैं?
o: Pure functional segments of ribose sugars and structural lipids.
Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) molecules and specialized proteins.
Complex amino acid linkages combined with porous cell wall elements.
High-density adenosine triphosphate molecules bounded by a membrane.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because ribose sugar is found in RNA, and lipids do not make up chromosomes. Option 2 is correct because the textbook states that chromosomes are composed of DNA and protein. DNA molecules contain the vital genetic blueprints necessary for constructing and organizing cells, while structural proteins (like histones) help wrap and pack the lengthy DNA strands tightly. Option 3 is incorrect because cell wall elements like cellulose have no structural role inside nuclear genetic material. Option 4 is incorrect because ATP is a loose chemical energy carrier, not a structural component of chromosomes.

qe: How are the functional segments of Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) molecules, which contain the essential operational information for cell construction, designated in biology?
qh: डिटॉक्सिरीबोन्यूक्लिक एसिड (DNA) अणुओं के कार्यात्मक खंड (functional segments), जिनमें कोशिका निर्माण के लिए आवश्यक परिचालन जानकारी होती है, जीव विज्ञान में किस नाम से जाने जाते हैं?
o: Chromatin networks
Nucleoids
Genes
Cisterns
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because chromatin represents the broad, unorganized macro-structural thread network of DNA and protein. Option 2 is incorrect because a nucleoid is the entire poorly defined nuclear region of a prokaryotic cell. Option 3 is correct because the source text explicitly defines the functional segments of DNA as genes [the physical and functional units of heredity that carry coded instructions for synthesizing proteins]. Option 4 is incorrect because cisterns are the parallel membrane-bound stacks that make up the Golgi apparatus.

qe: Which of the following cellular regions is structurally characterized as an undefined area containing only naked nucleic acids due to the complete absence of a nuclear membrane?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कोशिकीय क्षेत्र संरचनात्मक रूप से एक अपरिभाषित क्षेत्र के रूप में जाना जाता है जिसमें परमाणु झिल्ली (nuclear membrane) की पूर्ण अनुपस्थिति के कारण केवल नग्न न्यूक्लिक अम्ल होते हैं?
o: Eukaryotic Cytoplasm
Prokaryotic Nucleoid
Membranous Vesicle
Golgi Cistern stack
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because the eukaryotic cytoplasm is a highly organized fluid matrix surrounding a well-defined membrane-bound nucleus. Option 2 is correct because in primitive organisms like bacteria, the nuclear region lacks a protective lipid bilayer covering. This undefined nuclear region containing only bare genetic material is termed a nucleoid [the irregular-shaped region within a prokaryotic cell that contains all or most of the genetic material]. Such organisms are classified as prokaryotes. Option 3 is incorrect because a vesicle is a small membrane-bound transport pouch. Option 4 is incorrect because a cistern is a structural component of the Golgi apparatus involved in secretion, not genetic storage.

qe: How do photosynthetic prokaryotic bacteria structurally arrange their light-capturing chlorophyll molecules in the complete absence of advanced eukaryotic plastids?
qh: प्रकाश-संश्लेषण करने वाले प्रोकेरियोटिक बैक्टीरिया (photosynthetic prokaryotic bacteria) उन्नत यूकेरियोटिक प्लास्टिड्स की पूर्ण अनुपस्थिति में अपने प्रकाश-ग्रहण करने वाले क्लोरोफिल अणुओं को संरचनात्मक रूप से कैसे व्यवस्थित करते हैं?
o: Chlorophyll is associated with internal membranous vesicles.
Chlorophyll molecules float freely inside the double-layered nuclear membrane pores.
Chlorophyll is tightly bound to the structural proteins of the rigid cell wall.
Chlorophyll is concentrated exclusively within the dense stacks of Golgi cisterns.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is correct because the source text highlights a key evolutionary exception: the chlorophyll in photosynthetic prokaryotic bacteria is associated with simple membranous vesicles [bag-like structures formed by infoldings of the plasma membrane]. They completely lack complex, highly organized double-membrane organelles like chloroplast plastids [specialized plant organelles responsible for running photosynthesis]. Option 2 is incorrect because prokaryotes lack a nuclear membrane altogether. Option 3 is incorrect because cell walls provide mechanical protection and do not bind photosynthetic pigments. Option 4 is incorrect because prokaryotes do not possess membrane-bound organelles like the Golgi apparatus.

qe: Why do viruses fail to exhibit any formal characteristics of life or metabolic activity until they successfully infiltrate a living host organism?
qh: विषाणु (viruses) तब तक जीवन या चयापचय गतिविधि के किसी भी औपचारिक लक्षण को प्रदर्शित करने में क्यों विफल रहते हैं जब तक कि वे एक जीवित मेजबान जीव (host organism) में सफलतापूर्वक घुसपैठ नहीं कर लेते?
o: They contain complex sugars that require immediate active digestion by extracellular fluids.
They completely lack any structural biological membranes and must use the host's cellular machinery.
Their internal chromatin material is permanently locked in a dividing chromosome state.
They actively synthesize powerful digestive enzymes that break down their own capsular structures.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is a distractor; viruses do not possess complex sugars requiring external structural digestion. Option 2 is correct because the textbook notes that the profound significance of biological membranes is illustrated by viruses. Viruses lack any form of cellular membranes and internal metabolic machinery. Consequently, they remain inert chemical complexes showing no life signs until they enter a living cell body and hijack its cellular machinery to multiply. Option 3 is incorrect because viruses do not possess organized cellular nuclei or eukaryotic chromatin-chromosome cycles. Option 4 describes an autolytic process similar to lysosomal bursting, which does not apply to viral particles.

qe: What is the primary biochemical function executed by the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER), and what specific structural entity gives it its characteristic rough appearance?
qh: खुरदरी अंतःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका (RER) द्वारा निष्पादित प्राथमिक जैव-रासायनिक कार्य क्या है, और कौन सी विशिष्ट संरचनात्मक इकाई इसे इसकी खुरदरी उपस्थिति प्रदान करती है?
o: Detoxification of drugs fueled by parallel lipid cisterns.
Protein manufacture executed by ribosomes attached to its membrane surface.
Complex carbohydrate synthesis managed by isolated internal vacuoles.
Active transport of cellular sap controlled by specialized nuclear pores.
e: Explanation: Option 1 describes the function of the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) in vertebrate liver cells, not the RER. Option 2 is correct because the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum looks rough under a microscope due to the attachment of tiny granular particles called ribosomes [the cellular macromolecular machines responsible for protein translation] on its surface. The RER acts as the primary site for protein manufacture before dispatching them via transport channels. Option 3 is incorrect because carbohydrate modification occurs mainly in the Golgi apparatus. Option 4 is incorrect because nuclear pores are part of the nuclear envelope, not the endoplasmic reticulum system.

qe: The cellular process of 'membrane biogenesis' relies on the coordinated metabolic output of the endoplasmic reticulum. What does this process fundamentally involve?
qh: कोशकीय प्रक्रिया 'झिल्ली जीवजनन' (membrane biogenesis) अंतःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका के समन्वित चयापचय आउटपुट पर निर्भर करती है। इस प्रक्रिया में मौलिक रूप से क्या शामिल है?
o: The breakdown of dense cellulosic walls by powerful lysosomal digestive enzymes.
The utilization of manufactured proteins and lipids to construct the cell membrane.
The active accumulation of mineral electrolytes inside the central plant vacuole.
The mechanical expansion of nuclear pores to allow chromosome translocation.
e: Explanation: Option 1 describes cellular autolysis or degradation, which is opposite to membrane creation. Option 2 is correct because the endoplasmic reticulum manufactures crucial organic macromolecules: RER synthesizes proteins and SER synthesizes lipids. A portion of these newly made proteins and lipids are directly utilized to build and repair the cell's plasma membrane. This biological assembly process is known as membrane biogenesis [the structural synthesis of biological membranes from their constituent lipid and protein parts]. Option 3 describes vacuolar turgor maintenance, not membrane assembly. Option 4 is a fabricated distracter involving structural chromosome movement.

qe: In the liver cells of vertebrates, what crucial physiological role is performed by the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)?
qh: कशेरुकी प्राणियों (vertebrates) की यकृत कोशिकाओं (liver cells) में, चिकनी अंतःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका (SER) द्वारा कौन सी महत्वपूर्ण शारीरिक भूमिका निभाई जाती है?
o: The packaging and dispatching of genetic chromatin thread masses.
The detoxification of many poisons and drugs entering the animal body.
The structural synthesis of rigid, protective plant cell walls.
The generation of adenosine triphosphate via deeply folded inner membranes.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because chromatin packing is managed inside the nucleus by histones, not the SER. Option 2 is correct because the text highlights a critical metabolic exception: within the specialized liver cells [hepatocytes] of vertebrate animals, the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum plays a central role in detoxifying harmful xenobiotics, poisons, and clinical drugs, rendering them water-soluble for excretion. Option 3 is incorrect because animal liver cells do not contain cell walls or synthesize cellulose. Option 4 describes the function of mitochondrial cristae folds, not endoplasmic tubules.

qe: Biologist Camillo Golgi revolutionized the study of neurology by developing a specialized staining technique referred to as the 'black reaction'. Which chemical solution forms the base of this method?
qh: जीवविज्ञानी कैमिलो गोल्गी ने 'ब्लैक रिएक्शन' (black reaction) नामक एक विशिष्ट धुंधला (staining) तकनीक विकसित करके तंत्रिका विज्ञान के अध्ययन में क्रांति ला दी। कौन सा रासायनिक घोल इस पद्धति का आधार बनता है?
o: A concentrated copper sulfate organic extraction
A weak solution of silver nitrate
A saturated fluid mix of safranin and iodine
A basic aqueous solution of methylene blue
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because copper sulfate is not used in the classical Golgi method. Option 2 is correct because, as detailed in the biographical note, Camillo Golgi developed a revolutionary staining method termed the 'black reaction' which utilizes a weak solution of silver nitrate ($AgNO_3$). This technique allows the clear visualization of individual nerve structures and their delicate microscopic ramifications [intricate branch-like extensions of neural processes] against a clear background. Option 3 and Option 4 are incorrect because safranin, iodine, and methylene blue are standard tissue stains, not the base of the historical 'black reaction'.

qe: What is the structural relationship and functional role of the Golgi apparatus in connection with the materials synthesized near the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)?
qh: अंतःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका (ER) के पास संश्लेषित पदार्थों के संबंध में गोल्गी उपकरण (Golgi apparatus) का संरचनात्मक संबंध और कार्यात्मक भूमिका क्या है?
o: It completely destroys the ER proteins using powerful alkaline digestive enzymes.
It acts as a system to store, modify, package, and dispatch ER products to various targets.
It serves as a site for active genetic DNA replication during cellular reproduction.
It mechanically pumps excess fluid out of the cell via contractile vesicles.
e: Explanation: Option 1 describes lysosomal degradation rather than standard Golgi packaging. Option 2 is correct because the Golgi apparatus consists of stacked membrane-bound cisterns that often link with the ER membrane system. The proteins and lipids synthesized near the ER are transferred to the Golgi apparatus, where they undergo storage, chemical modification [such as processing simple sugars into complex sugars], packaging, and final dispatch to intracellular or extracellular targets. It is also involved in making lysosomes. Option 3 is incorrect because DNA replication occurs exclusively inside the nucleus or nucleoid. Option 4 describes vacuolar osmoregulation, not Golgi trafficking.

qe: Why are Lysosomes metaphorically designated as the 'suicide bags' of a cell during conditions of severe structural damage or metabolic disturbance?
qh: गंभीर संरचनात्मक क्षति या चयापचय गड़बड़ी (metabolic disturbance) की स्थिति में लाइसोसोम (Lysosomes) को लाक्षणिक रूप से कोशिका की 'आत्मघाती थैली' (suicide bags) क्यों कहा जाता है?
o: They actively pump out all structural ATP molecules into the external tissue fluids.
They may burst, causing their powerful internal digestive enzymes to digest their own cell.
They compress the nucleus until the chromatin material undergoes mechanical lysis.
They transform into rigid chromoplast structures that block nutritional intake.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because lysosomes contain hydrolase enzymes, not ATP pumps. Option 2 is correct because lysosomes function as the cell's waste disposal system, filled with powerful digestive enzymes manufactured by the RER. When a cell undergoes severe metabolic trauma or structural damage, these membrane sacs may burst, releasing their internal enzymes which then digest the entire cell's organic contents. This process leads to autolysis [self-destruction of a cell by its own enzymes]. Option 3 is incorrect because lysosomal action is chemical hydrolysis, not mechanical compression of the nucleus. Option 4 is an inaccurate combination involving plastids.

qe: Mitochondria are unique organelles because they can manufacture some of their own proteins independently. What structural components allow them to accomplish this?
qh: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया (Mitochondria) अद्वितीय अंगक (organelles) हैं क्योंकि वे स्वतंत्र रूप से अपने स्वयं के कुछ प्रोटीन का निर्माण कर सकते हैं। कौन से संरचनात्मक घटक उन्हें इसे पूरा करने की अनुमति देते हैं?
o: A single porous membrane coat combined with external nuclear pores.
The presence of their own distinct DNA molecules and internal ribosomes.
Deeply folded outer walls containing vast arrays of complex sugars.
A matrix filled entirely with active lysosomal digestive enzymes.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because mitochondria possess a double-membrane envelope, not a single porous coat, and do not rely on nuclear pores for independent synthesis. Option 2 is correct because the text points out that mitochondria are strange organelles because they contain their own genomic DNA [independent extranuclear genetic material] and their own ribosomes [70S cellular protein-building machinery]. This enables them to transcribe and translate a subset of necessary mitochondrial proteins without relying completely on the cell's nucleus. Option 3 is incorrect because the inner membrane is folded (cristae), not the outer wall, and folds create surface area for ATP reactions, not sugar arrays. Option 4 describes a lysosome, not the mitochondrial matrix.

qe: Which of the following accurately matches the two distinct types of plant plastids with their primary intracellular operational functions?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकल्प पादप प्लास्टिड्स (plant plastids) के दो अलग-अलग प्रकारों को उनके प्राथमिक अंतःकोशकीय परिचालन कार्यों (intracellular operational functions) के साथ सटीक रूप से सुमेलित करता है?
o: Chromoplasts (ATP generation) and Leucoplasts (gaseous carbon dioxide exchange)
Chromoplasts (coloured plastids for photosynthesis/pigments) and Leucoplasts (storage of starch, oils, and proteins)
Chloroplasts (waste disposal via bursting) and Chromoplasts (membrane biogenesis)
Leucoplasts (fluid turgidity maintenance) and Chloroplasts (silver nitrate black reactions)
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because mitochondria generate ATP, and plastids do not manage stomatal gas exchange. Option 2 is correct because the source text divides plastids into chromoplasts [coloured plastids containing pigments like chlorophyll, yellow, or orange, crucial for running photosynthesis] and leucoplasts [colorless or white plastids whose primary cellular role is the biochemical storage of nutrient materials like starch granules, oils, and protein granules]. Option 3 incorrectly mixes lysosomal waste disposal and ER membrane biogenesis with plastids. Option 4 incorrectly links vacuolar turgidity and Golgi staining with plant plastids.

qe: The central vacuole of a mature plant cell can occupy up to 50-90% of the internal volume. What fluid fills this structure, and what functional attributes does it provide to the cell?
qh: एक परिपक्व पादप कोशिका (plant cell) का केंद्रीय रिक्तिका (central vacuole) आंतरिक आयतन का 50-90% तक घेर सकता है। कौन सा तरल इस संरचना को भरता है, और यह कोशिका को कौन से कार्यात्मक गुण प्रदान करता है?
o: Highly concentrated silver nitrate fluid; providing dynamic bio-electric nerve impulses.
Cell sap fluid; providing essential hydrostatic turgidity and mechanical rigidity.
Pure liquid lipids; driving the continuous biogenesis of the outer cell wall.
Active digestive enzymes; functioning as an aggressive cytoplasmic suicide bag.
e: Explanation: Option 1 describes nerve tissue properties and silver nitrate staining, which are absent in plant vacuoles. Option 2 is correct because plant vacuoles are large vesicles completely filled with a fluid solution called cell sap [an aqueous solution containing amino acids, sugars, organic acids, mineral salts, and proteins]. This internal fluid volume exerts hydrostatic pressure outward against the cytoplasm and cell wall, providing vital turgidity [swollen water-filled state] and rigidity [mechanical stiffness] to sustain the plant tissue architecture. Option 3 is incorrect because vacuoles store diverse water-soluble compounds, not pure liquid lipids for cell walls. Option 4 describes the destructive function of a lysosome rather than standard vacuolar storage.

qe: Why does a macromolecular assembly containing isolated genetic material and enzymes fail to meet the absolute biological criteria for independent living as established by the cell theory?
qh: कोशिका सिद्धांत द्वारा स्थापित स्वतंत्र जीवन के पूर्ण जैविक मानदंडों को पूरा करने में पृथक आनुवंशिक सामग्री और एंजाइमों से युक्त एक मैक्रोमोलेक्युलर असेंबली क्यों विफल हो जाती है?
o: It lacks the capability to synthesize non-polar saturated lipids within extracellular fluid matrices.
Anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent existence and life functions.
The absence of flagellar hook proteins restricts the mechanical transformation of the envelope.
Isolated chromatin material undergoes structural ionization when exposed to light photons.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because lipid synthesis within extracellular fluids is not a metric for independent life status. Option 2 is correct because the text explicitly establishes that unicellular organisms demonstrate independent existence and perform essential life functions. Crucially, anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living, making the integrated cellular architecture the fundamental structural and functional unit of life. Option 3 is incorrect because flagella relate strictly to motility [the capacity of a cell to move spontaneously], not the baseline definition of life. Option 4 is an scientifically inaccurate distractor involving chromatin ionization [the conversion of DNA-protein structures into charged ions under radiation].

qe: Which specific evolutionary and structural exception challenges the universal rule that all prokaryotic cells possess a rigid, protective cell wall surrounding their plasma membrane?
qh: कौन सा विशिष्ट विकासवादी और संरचनात्मक अपवाद इस सार्वभौमिक नियम को चुनौती देता है कि सभी प्रोकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में उनकी प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के चारों ओर एक कठोर, सुरक्षात्मक कोशिका भित्ति होती है?
o: Cyanobacteria (Blue-green algae)
Mycoplasma
PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms) with capsule sheets
Gram-positive Bacillus variants
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because cyanobacteria possess a complete cell wall containing specialized accessory photosynthetic pigments. Option 2 is correct because the source text notes a critical structural exception: all prokaryotes have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane except for mycoplasma. Mycoplasma represents the smallest cells (0.3 µm) and completely lacks a bounding wall, making them highly flexible but structurally unique among prokaryotes. Option 3 is incorrect because while PPLO are related to mycoplasmas, the text explicitly marks 'mycoplasma' as the distinct entry lacking a wall boundary. Option 4 is incorrect because Bacillus variants are standard rod-shaped bacteria with highly organized peptidoglycan cell walls.

qe: The historical evolution of the Cell Theory reached its definitive final shape in 1855. What specific limitation of the classical Schleiden-Schwann model was resolved by Rudolf Virchow?
qh: कोशिका सिद्धांत (Cell Theory) का ऐतिहासिक विकास 1855 में अपने अंतिम रूप में पहुंचा। श्लेडेन-श्वान के क्लासिक मॉडल की किस विशिष्ट सीमा को रुडोल्फ विरचो द्वारा हल किया गया था?
o: The dynamic discovery of the hydrophobic lipid bilayer within animal tissues.
The physical mapping of nuclear pore pathways connecting the matrix.
The explanation of the specific mechanism detailing how new cells are actually formed.
The formulation of chemical staining procedures utilizing silver nitrate solutions.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because the lipid bilayer structure was deduced much later via biochemical investigations, not by Virchow. Option 2 is incorrect because nuclear pore mapping required advanced electron microscopy. Option 3 is correct because Schleiden and Schwann's original theory did not explain how new cells were formed. Rudolf Virchow (1855) first explained that cells divide and new cells arise from pre-existing cells via cellular division, conceptualized as 'Omnis cellula-e cellula', which gave the cell theory its complete modern shape. Option 4 describes Camillo Golgi's chemical staining advancement, not Virchow's cellular lineage theory.

qe: A historical researcher analyzes the baseline conclusions of Theodore Schwann (1839). Which of the following represents a structural deduction made by Schwann through his work on plant tissues?
qh: एक ऐतिहासिक शोधकर्ता थियोडोर श्वान (1839) के आधारभूत निष्कर्षों का विश्लेषण करता है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा श्वान द्वारा पादप ऊतकों पर अपने कार्य के माध्यम से निकाला गया एक संरचनात्मक निष्कर्ष प्रस्तुत करता है?
o: The cell wall represents a completely unique character specific only to plant cells.
Animal cells lack a plasma membrane and rely entirely on loose mucosal matrices.
All plant tissues arise from the division of specialized pre-existing internal vacuoles.
Ribosomes are uniquely absent within the cytoplasm of botanical organisms.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is correct because Schwann, despite being a British Zoologist, examined plant tissues as well and concluded that the presence of a cell wall is a unique character of the plant cells. Based on this, he proposed the overarching hypothesis that the bodies of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells. Option 2 is incorrect because Schwann discovered that animal cells explicitly possess a thin outer layer, known today as the plasma membrane. Option 3 is incorrect because Virchow discovered cell lineage, not Schwann working on vacuoles. Option 4 is incorrect because ribosomes are universally present in all active living cells.

qe: Which of the following cellular structures represents a non-membrane bound organelle found universally across both prokaryotic and eukaryotic lines, as well as inside specific organelles?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी कोशिकीय संरचना प्रोकेरियोटिक और यूकेरियोटिक दोनों प्रकार की कोशिकाओं में, साथ ही विशिष्ट अंगकों (organelles) के भीतर सार्वभौमिक रूप से पाया जाने वाला एक गैर-झिल्लीबद्ध अंगक (non-membrane bound organelle) है?
o: Centrosome
Mesosome
Ribosome
Peroxisome
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because the centrosome is a non-membrane bound organelle restricted specifically to animal cells to aid cell division. Option 2 is incorrect because mesosomes are specialized membranous infoldings unique to prokaryotes. Option 3 is correct because the source text explicitly notes that ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells—both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic. Furthermore, they are not confined to the cytoplasm; they are also located inside two specific eukaryotic organelles: chloroplasts (in plants) and mitochondria, as well as on the rough ER surface. Option 4 is incorrect because peroxisomes are membrane-bound organelles belonging to the broader eukaryotic cytoplasmic matrix.

qe: If a bacterium is classified as 'Gram-negative' during a standard microbiological analysis, what structural feature of its cell envelope fundamentally dictates this specific staining response?
qh: यदि एक मानक सूक्ष्मजैविक विश्लेषण के दौरान एक बैक्टीरिया को 'ग्राम-नकारात्मक' (Gram-negative) के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है, तो उसके सेल लिफाफे (cell envelope) की कौन सी संरचनात्मक विशेषता मौलिक रूप से इस विशिष्ट धुंधला प्रतिक्रिया (staining response) को निर्धारित करती है?
o: The complete absence of a functional inner plasma membrane.
The structural differences in the multi-layered cell envelope and its interaction with the Gram stain.
The presence of specialized circular plasmid DNA within the outermost slime layer.
The direct integration of non-membranous phosphate inclusion bodies into the capsule.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because all functional bacteria possess a plasma membrane to interact with the outside world. Option 2 is correct because bacteria are classified into Gram-positive and Gram-negative groups based on the structural differences in their cell envelopes [the tightly bound three-layered protective unit comprising glycocalyx, cell wall, and plasma membrane] and the specific manner in which they respond to the staining procedure developed by Christian Gram. Gram-negative cells do not retain the primary crystal violet complex due to these envelope variations. Option 3 is incorrect because plasmids are internal cytoplasmic DNA elements, not part of the structural staining mechanism of the envelope. Option 4 is incorrect because inclusion bodies lie free within the inner cytoplasm, having no relation to outer envelope staining.

qe: What physical distinction differentiates a bacterial glycocalyx layer described as a 'slime layer' from one designated as a 'capsule'?
qh: एक 'स्लाइम लेयर' (slime layer) के रूप में वर्णित बैक्टीरियल ग्लाइकोकैलिक्स परत को 'कैप्सूल' (capsule) के रूप में नामित परत से क्या भौतिक अंतर अलग करता है?
o: A slime layer is composed of structural cellulose, whereas a capsule contains only calcium pectate granules.
A slime layer is a loose sheath, while a capsule is characterized as a thick and tough layer.
A slime layer facilitates active flagellar motility, whereas a capsule locks the cell into a non-motile phase.
A slime layer contains highly organized 70S ribosomes, while a capsule lacks all macromolecular machinery.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because bacterial cell walls contain peptidoglycan matrices, not pure plant cellulose or middle lamella calcium pectate. Option 2 is correct because the text explicitly states that the outermost glycocalyx layer of the bacterial cell envelope differs in composition and thickness among different bacteria. It manifests as a loose sheath called the slime layer in some, while in others it forms a thick and tough structural layer designated as the capsule. Option 3 is incorrect because flagella sprout from the cell wall through the envelope to govern motility [spontaneous biological movement], which is distinct from glycocalyx density. Option 4 is incorrect because ribosomes are strictly intracellular structures and are never located in the extracellular glycocalyx layers.

qe: Prokaryotic bacteria lack advanced eukaryotic organelles, yet they carry out respiration, cell wall formation, and DNA distribution to daughter cells. Which specialized prokaryotic structure executes these coordinated processes?
qh: प्रोकेरियोटिक बैक्टीरिया में उन्नत यूकेरियोटिक अंगकों का अभाव होता है, फिर भी वे श्वसन, कोशिका भित्ति निर्माण और संतति कोशिकाओं में DNA वितरण जैसी समन्वित प्रक्रियाओं को अंजाम देते हैं। कौन सी विशिष्ट प्रोकेरियोटिक संरचना इन प्रक्रियाओं को निष्पादित करती है?
o: Extracellular bristle-like fimbriae fibres
The specialized circular plasmid DNA
The mesosome, formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell
The non-membranous cyanophycean inclusion bodies
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because fimbriae are small surface fibres used solely for attachment to rocks or host tissues. Option 2 is incorrect because plasmids carry antibiotic resistance genes but do not serve as respiratory or structural membrane platforms. Option 3 is correct because the text highlights that the mesosome is a characteristic, specialized differentiated form of cell membrane found as infoldings (vesicles, tubules, lamellae) in prokaryotes. They actively help in cell wall formation, DNA replication, cellular respiration, secretion processes, and increasing the functional surface area and enzymatic content of the membrane. Option 4 is incorrect because cyanophycean granules are passive reserve materials stored inside the cytoplasm.

qe: A microbiologist isolates a motile bacterium from a freshwater stream. If they isolate the longest portion of its structural motility apparatus extending from the cell surface to the outside, what part are they analyzing?
qh: एक सूक्ष्मजीवविज्ञानी एक मीठे पानी की धारा से एक गतिशील (motile) बैक्टीरिया को अलग करता है। यदि वे सेल की सतह से बाहर की ओर फैले इसके संरचनात्मक गतिशीलता उपकरण (motility apparatus) के सबसे लंबे हिस्से को अलग करते हैं, तो वे किसका विश्लेषण कर रहे हैं?
o: The basal body anchored in the inner membrane
The flexible hook connecting the envelope layers
The filament of the flagellum
The elongated tubular pilis made of special protein
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because the basal body is the internal anchoring core embedded within the cell envelope. Option 2 is incorrect because the hook is the short connecting joint between the filament and basal body. Option 3 is correct because bacterial flagella [thin filamentous extensions from the cell wall governing motility] are composed of three parts: filament, hook, and basal body. The text explicitly notes that the filament is the longest portion and extends from the cell surface to the outside. Option 4 is incorrect because pili are surface structures involved in conjugation or attachment, not flagellar motility parts.

qe: What is the structural composition of the functional prokaryotic ribosome, and where is it primarily localized within a bacterial cell?
qh: कार्यात्मक प्रोकेरियोटिक राइबोसोम की संरचनात्मक संरचना क्या है, और यह मुख्य रूप से एक बैक्टीरियल कोशिका के भीतर कहाँ स्थित होता है?
o: An 80S unit localized strictly inside the double-layered nuclear envelope matrix.
A 70S unit composed of 50S and 30S subunits, associated with the plasma membrane.
A 60S unit composed of distinct non-functional phosphate inclusion segments.
A 100S linear polysome chain attached directly to the extracellular capsule.
None of the above / उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because prokaryotes lack an 80S ribosome and have no nuclear envelope. Option 2 is correct because the source text states that prokaryotic ribosomes are about 15 nm by 20 nm in size, are associated with the plasma membrane of the cell, and are made of two subunits—50S and 30S units—which together form the characteristic 70S prokaryotic ribosome [where 'S' represents the Svedberg unit, a metric of sedimentation rate during centrifugation]. Option 3 is incorrect because a 60S unit is a subunit of eukaryotic 80S ribosomes, not prokaryotic models. Option 4 is incorrect because polysomes are mRNA-ribosome complexes inside the cytoplasm, never extracellular.

qe: During active protein synthesis, multiple ribosomes in a prokaryotic cell are often observed attached to a single strand of messenger RNA (mRNA). What is this cellular architecture called?
qh: सक्रिय प्रोटीन संश्लेषण के दौरान, एक प्रोकेरियोटिक कोशिका में कई राइबोसोम अक्सर मैसेंजर RNA (mRNA) के एक एकल स्ट्रैंड से जुड़े हुए देखे जाते हैं। इस कोशिकीय संरचना को क्या कहा जाता है?
o: A plasmid transformant complex
A chromatophore pigment vesicle
A polyribosome or polysome
An unencapsulated inclusion body
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because plasmid transformation relates to foreign DNA uptake, not mRNA translation. Option 2 is incorrect because chromatophores are internal pigment-containing membrane extensions found in cyanobacteria. Option 3 is correct because the text states that several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA to form a distinct chain called a polyribosome or polysome. The individual ribosomes of a polysome simultaneously translate the mRNA strand into proteins, increasing synthetic efficiency. Option 4 is incorrect because inclusion bodies are static storage structures for reserve materials, not active translational complexes.

qe: Which of the following reserve materials stored inside prokaryotic cells represents a distinct structural exception by being associated with gas vacuoles in specific photosynthetic bacterial lines?
qh: प्रोकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं के भीतर संग्रहीत निम्नलिखित आरक्षित सामग्रियों में से कौन सा विशिष्ट प्रकाश-संश्लेषण करने वाले बैक्टीरियल उपभेदों में गैस रिक्तिकाओं (gas vacuoles) से जुड़े होने के कारण एक अलग संरचनात्मक अपवाद प्रस्तुत करता है?
o: Phosphate granules
Glycogen granules
Gas vacuoles found in blue-green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria
Suberized calcium carbonate crystals
e: Explanation: Option 1 and Option 2 are incorrect because phosphate and glycogen granules are standard solid inclusion bodies that lie free in the cytoplasm without gas properties. Option 3 is correct because the source text distinguishes standard free membrane-less inclusion bodies (like phosphate, cyanophycean, and glycogen granules) from gas vacuoles. Gas vacuoles [specialized proteinaceous structures providing buoyancy] are uniquely found in blue-green, purple, and green photosynthetic bacteria to help them adjust their vertical position in aquatic columns. Option 4 describes algal cell wall mineral elements, which are completely irrelevant to prokaryotic inclusion bodies.

qe: Chemical analyses of human red blood cells (RBCs) in the 1950s allowed scientists to deduce the foundational architecture of the plasma membrane. What specific lipid arrangement protects the hydrophobic tails from the aqueous environment?
qh: 1950 के दशक में मानव लाल रक्त कोशिकाओं (RBCs) के रासायनिक विश्लेषणों ने वैज्ञानिकों को प्लाज्मा झिल्ली की आधारभूत संरचना का अनुमान लगाने की अनुमति दी। कौन सी विशिष्ट लिपिड व्यवस्था हाइड्रोफोबिक पूंछों (hydrophobic tails) को जलीय वातावरण से बचाती है?
o: A single layer where hydrophobic heads face the cytosolic matrix directly.
A lipid bilayer arranged with polar heads outward and hydrophobic tails toward the inner part.
A random suspension of cholesterol micelle spheres lacking polar alignment.
A rigid protein envelope that completely blocks water molecules from the lipid core.
e: Explanation: Option 1 describes an chemically unstable monolayer configuration that cannot exist as a structural biological cell barrier. Option 2 is correct because chemical studies on erythrocyte [red blood cell] membranes demonstrated that the major lipids are phospholipids arranged in a bilayer [a double layer of lipid molecules]. The polar (hydrophilic) heads face the outer aqueous sides, while the nonpolar, hydrophobic tails composed of saturated hydrocarbons are oriented toward the inner part, protecting them from the aqueous environment. Option 3 is incorrect because cholesterol is an interspersed stabilizing lipid component, not the primary bilayer matrix. Option 4 is incorrect because proteins do not form a solid blocking envelope; they are embedded fluidly according to the mosaic model.

qe: Biochemical investigations show that the ratio of protein to lipid varies considerably across cell types. What are the specific percentage compositions observed within the membrane of a human erythrocyte?
qh: जैव-रासायनिक जांच दर्शाती है कि प्रोटीन और लिपिड का अनुपात विभिन्न कोशिकाओं में काफी भिन्न होता है। मानव एरिथ्रोसाइट (erythrocyte) की झिल्ली के भीतर देखे जाने वाले विशिष्ट प्रतिशत संयोजन क्या हैं?
o: 80 per cent protein and 20 per cent carbohydrate structures
40 per cent protein and 52 per cent structural phospholipids
52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids
60 per cent cholesterol and 40 per cent peripheral proteins
e: Explanation: Option 1 and Option 2 are incorrect because they present inaccurate scrambled ratios that contradict established experimental data. Option 3 is correct because the textbook provides a concrete quantitative metric: in human beings, the membrane of the erythrocyte (red blood cell) has a precise composition consisting of approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids, with the remainder composed of carbohydrates. Option 4 is a fabricated distractor maximizing cholesterol metrics far beyond biological reality.

qe: According to the Fluid Mosaic Model proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972, what physical property allows the lateral movement of proteins within the overall membrane bilayer?
qh: 1972 में सिंगर और निकोलसन द्वारा प्रस्तावित फ्लूइड मोज़ेक मॉडल (Fluid Mosaic Model) के अनुसार, कौन सा भौतिक गुण प्रोटीन को समग्र झिल्ली द्विसतह (bilayer) के भीतर पार्श्व गति (lateral movement) करने की अनुमति देता है?
o: The completely solid, static crystalline grid formed by peripheral carbohydrates.
The quasi-fluid nature of the lipid bilayer.
The active expenditure of ATP molecules by transmembrane carrier pumps.
The rigid mechanical counter-pressure generated by the primary cell wall.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because a static crystalline grid would completely lock proteins in place, preventing any lateral displacement. Option 2 is correct because the Fluid Mosaic Model explains that the lipid bilayer possesses a quasi-fluid nature [a semi-liquid state sharing properties of both fluids and crystalline solids]. This specific fluidity enables the lateral movement of integrated proteins within the overall bilayer, a dynamic quality measured directly as membrane fluidity. Option 3 is incorrect because lateral protein drifting is a passive physical property driven by lipid fluidity, not active ATP pumping. Option 4 describes plant wall attributes that do not regulate internal membrane lipid physics.

qe: Why do polar molecules require specialized carrier proteins to accomplish transport across the plasma membrane down their concentration gradient?
qh: ध्रुवीय अणुओं (polar molecules) को अपनी सांद्रता प्रवणता के अनुकूल प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के पार परिवहन पूरा करने के लिए विशिष्ट वाहक प्रोटीन (carrier proteins) की आवश्यकता क्यों होती है?
o: Polar molecules are chemically converted into solid chitin elements upon touching lipids.
They cannot pass through the nonpolar hydrophobic core of the lipid bilayer.
Polar molecules lack the thermal kinetic energy needed to undergo simple diffusion.
They are actively repelled by the calcium pectate layer of the middle lamella.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is a scientifically inaccurate distractor involving chitin transformations. Option 2 is correct because the interior core of the plasma membrane bilayer consists of nonpolar, hydrophobic fatty acid tails. Polar molecules [molecules with partial electrical charges due to unequal electron distribution] are water-soluble and cannot dissolve in or cross this lipid core. Therefore, they require a facilitated transporter or carrier protein [a transmembrane protein that assists specific molecules across a biological membrane] to cross without spending energy. Option 3 is incorrect because polar molecules possess identical thermal kinetic energy to neutral solutes. Option 4 describes an extracellular plant structural wall boundary that does not dictate internal membrane transport laws.

qe: Which of the following transport mechanisms represents a highly specific energy-dependent process where ions are moved across the membrane *against* their concentration gradient?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा परिवहन तंत्र (transport mechanism) एक अत्यधिक विशिष्ट ऊर्जा-निर्भर प्रक्रिया का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है जहाँ आयनों को उनकी सांद्रता प्रवणता के *विपरीत* झिल्ली के पार ले जाया जाता है?
o: Simple passive diffusion of neutral solute particles
Osmotic flow of solvent water through selectively porous aquaporins
The $Na^+/K^+$ Pump operating via ATP utilization
Facilitated lateral drifting across peripheral protein layers
e: Explanation: Option 1 and Option 2 are incorrect because simple diffusion and osmosis are strictly passive transport mechanisms [movements driven by existing gradients that require no metabolic energy input]. Option 3 is correct because the text explicitly defines active transport as an energy-dependent process in which specific ions or molecules are pumped across the plasma membrane against their concentration gradient (from lower to higher concentration) via the utilization of ATP energy currency. A classic physiological example provided is the $Na^+/K^+$ Pump [Sodium-Potassium Adenosine Triphosphatase]. Option 4 describes passive lateral movement within the fluid plane, not active transport against gradients.

qe: Algae possess a unique cell wall composition that distinguishes them from higher terrestrial plants. Which of the following sets of chemical constituents is specific to the algal cell wall?
qh: शैवाल (Algae) में एक अद्वितीय कोशिका भित्ति संरचना होती है जो उन्हें उच्च स्थलीय पौधों से अलग करती है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा रासायनिक घटकों का समूह शैवाल की कोशिका भित्ति के लिए विशिष्ट है?
o: Cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and structural proteins
Cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals like calcium carbonate
Chitin polymers integrated with high-density saturated sterols
Peptidoglycan matrices linked with teichoic acid slime networks
e: Explanation: Option 1 describes the standard chemical composition of typical terrestrial higher plant cell walls. Option 2 is correct because the source text explicitly highlights a comparative exception: algae have a cell wall made of cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals like calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$). This distinguishes them from other plants whose walls consist of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins. Option 3 describes fungal wall and animal membrane compositions. Option 4 describes prokaryotic bacterial cell wall chemistry.

qe: What specific layer holds or glues neighbouring plant cells together, and what is its primary chemical constituent?
qh: कौन सी विशिष्ट परत पड़ोसी पादप कोशिकाओं को एक साथ पकड़ती या चिपकाती (glues) है, और इसका प्राथमिक रासायनिक घटक क्या है?
o: The primary cell wall composed entirely of hydrophobic hemicellulose.
The secondary inner wall made of highly flexible peripheral proteins.
The middle lamella composed mainly of calcium pectate.
The plasmodesmata channel lined with structural phospholipid sheets.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because the primary wall is the initial expandable layer of a young cell, not the glue between separate cells. Option 2 is incorrect because the secondary wall is formed later on the inner side as the cell matures to add rigid support. Option 3 is correct because the middle lamella is a distinct intercellular layer composed mainly of calcium pectate [a salt of pectic acid that acts as a structural cementing agent]. Its primary biological function is to glue and hold neighbouring plant cell walls firmly together. Option 4 is incorrect because plasmodesmata are microscopic cytoplasmic channels that traverse the cell wall to connect adjacent cells, not the cementing matrix itself.

qe: Why are mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes excluded from the 'Endomembrane System' of eukaryotic cells despite being membrane-bound organelles scattered within the cytoplasm?
qh: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया, क्लोरोप्लास्ट और पेरोक्सीसोम को साइटोप्लाज्म के भीतर बिखरे हुए झिल्लीबद्ध अंगक होने के बावजूद यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं के 'एंडोमेम्ब्रेन सिस्टम' (Endomembrane System) से क्यों बाहर रखा गया है?
o: They lack any functional internal enzymatic matrix or protein structures.
Their metabolic functions are not coordinated with the components like ER and Golgi complex.
They carry out active transport exclusively through nonpolar lipid channels.
They display a prokaryotic 70S ribosome attached directly to their outer coats.
e: Explanation: Option 1 is incorrect because these organelles contain extensive metabolic enzymes (e.g., ATP-synthase in mitochondria, RuBisCO in chloroplasts).
